headline: FAA grounds flights at all U.S. airports, citing communications issue
author: Liam Scott, Maegan Vazquez, Todd C. Frankel

paragraphs.text: The Federal Aviation Administration issued an unexpected nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, citing a communication issue.
“FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide updates,” the agency said in a statement. The FAA said its information was preliminary and subject to change.
Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy said on X that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop followed “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.”
This is the second national ground stop since Sept. 11, 2001. The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop in January 2023 over a systems outage.

About 3,115 flights were still inbound to U.S. airports at about 4:40 p.m. Eastern, according to flight-tracking platform AirNav Radar. These were the last planes to get off the ground before the ground stop.
At Los Angeles International Airport, a United Airlines gate agent announced to passengers that there had been a nationwide ground stop but said she did not know why.
Air traffic control audio pilots and air traffic controllers across the United States learned about the ground stop Friday afternoon.

“Why is there a ground stop?” a pilot asked Friday afternoon at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, according to air traffic control recordings on ATC.com. “We are not aware of a reason. We just know it’s indefinite and U.S.-wide,” an air traffic controller replied.
At Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, an air traffic controller told a Southwest Airlines pilot, “Just a heads up, we went into a national ground stop, all aircraft, with update unknown.”

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority said passengers should expect flight delays related to the ground stop, but Reagan National Airport and Washington Dulles International Airport remained open.

A United spokesperson said the airline was responding to the ground stop. United flights that are already airborne will continue, the spokesperson said, but new domestic flights will not depart while the ground stop remains in place.
“United will work with our customers to get them to their destinations once this issue is resolved,” the spokesperson said.
This is a developing news story and will be updated.
